note: THE DESKTOP ADMIN NAV BECOMES A RAIL WITH FLYOUTS. The founder, with seven ClickUp screenshots: 'instead of having all of the features in the sidebar, lets put the categories and when hovering over, to appear like in the screenshots attached' — and, asked whether that meant hover or click, 'both'. It rendered every permitted tab at once, in four collapsible headings inside one 232px column that scrolled internally. THE-332 OWNS the three files below and this is the state it leaves them in. MOBILE IS UNTOUCHED, as the founder asked ('in mobile stays the same for now'): MORE_GROUPS and the More sheet are byte-identical and pinned as such in this ticket's own suite, as are AdminEvents.tsx, AdminServices.tsx, AdminSms.tsx, AdminCommunity.tsx, UserMessages.tsx, firestore.rules, firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and layout.tsx. No permission gate moved, no npm dependency was added, and no theme token was minted — the eight sidebar variables THE-270 already bridged onto Harvest's own tokens are re-asserted, not extended.

entries.why: THE DESKTOP COLUMN IS NOW SIX ENTRIES, NOT TWENTY-THREE. Dashboard and Settings stay pinned outside the groups and are reachable in ONE action as icon-only rail buttons; the four groups (CONTENT, MINISTRY, BROADCASTING, GROW) became flyout triggers. `isSidebarCollapsed`, `collapsedGroups` and `toggleGroup` are GONE rather than disabled — the rail is permanently at `lg:w-[88px]`, the width this sidebar already used when collapsed, so 'collapse the sidebar' and 'collapse a heading' no longer name anything on screen, and the `title` attribute that was the old collapsed tooltip is replaced by an `aria-label` a keyboard and a screen reader can actually reach. No width is invented: the rail is the old collapsed width and the flyout is `w-64`, the old expanded width, which is sidebar.tsx's own SIDEBAR_WIDTH. `desktopSidebarGroups` and `visibleNavGroups` are untouched, so a group with no permitted tabs is still omitted whole and `library` is still `isSuperAdmin`-only. Each group advertises its permitted tabs on `data-nav-group-tabs` / `data-nav-group-labels` because a closed flyout unmounts its rows, and seven pre-existing entitlement guards read the nav by scanning the DOM; THE-332's own suite holds that advertised model equal to what the flyout renders, so it cannot become a comfortable lie. THE-327's budget of nine code-level colour literals is met EXACTLY — the rail's wordmark removed one and the new `RAIL_ACTIVE_INK` constant adds one back, so this ticket adds none. Every mobile class, the More sheet, the top bar and every screen mount are unchanged.

NEW. The flyout mechanism, built on the INSTALLED `ui/popover` — which is Base UI, not Radix, and already ships every part this needs: `openOnHover` on the trigger gives hover, the trigger is a real <button> so Enter/Space open it and Base UI moves focus into the popup and returns it on Escape, and `onOpenChange` reports WHY it changed ('trigger-press' vs 'trigger-hover') which is what lets a click PIN a flyout a hover would have closed. `hover-card` was REJECTED because it has no press semantics and therefore nothing to pin, and is documented for non-interactive preview content while these flyouts are the only way to reach 21 of the 23 tabs; `dropdown-menu` because its `menuitem` roving focus and typeahead would swallow single-letter keys and it closes on pointer-leave with no pin; `tooltip` because it is non-interactive by role, which IS the defect being fixed. Hover is gated on `(min-width: 1024px) and (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — three conditions, not a width, because on touch `:hover` fires on tap and then sticks — and the gate starts FALSE and is raised in an effect so SSR and the first client frame agree. It hardcodes no colour, renders no emoji, positions nothing itself and adds no dependency.

NEW, AND DELIBERATELY TINY. One map from a DESKTOP_NAV_GROUPS label to the lucide icon its rail entry wears. The rail holds the four GROUP LABELS rather than the ten most-used tabs: ClickUp's own rail is destinations, but in Harvest the groups ARE the destinations, and ranking tabs by 'most used' would have meant inventing a ranking this product has no usage data for and pushing thirteen tabs behind an overflow whose reachability is far harder to guarantee. With the groups in the rail every one of the 23 tabs sits in exactly one flyout. The icons reuse vocabulary the product already has — Church is what AdminChurches draws, Radio is what AdminLivestream draws — rather than minting a second one. It holds no colour, no width and no permission logic.
